comprehension_flags: A general reader may stumble on the specialist vocabulary carried over untranslated — "apophatic", "antinomies", "sublimated", "existentiation", "denouement", and the Latin "grosso modo" (rendered here as "wholesale") — none of which this pass is authorized to gloss inline.

chapters.title: The Discourse to Kumayl
editorial_queries: The source's forward references to "the second chapter" and "the third chapter" were recast as direct statements (worship's role in the quest for justice; remembrance as the quintessence of worship's fruits), since this edition's chapter scheme may not match the source's numbering — an editor should confirm the neighboring chapters still carry those topics.
comprehension_flags: The passage stacks many transliterated technical terms (zahir/batin, haqiqa/tahaqquq/tahqiq, tawhid, hawa, ikhlas) in close succession; each is glossed in place, but a first-time reader may still find the density demanding.
terminology_notes: hamaj raa — the gloss "the moth that hurls itself at any flame" should be standardized against the rendering used elsewhere in the book.

chapters.title: The Fruits of Certainty
comprehension_flags: A general reader may stumble on "scientistic," which is retained because "scientific" would alter the author's meaning (a critique of scientism, not of science).
terminology_notes: epistemology — kept verbatim on both occurrences ("epistemology of joy," "joyous epistemology") rather than paraphrased, to hold the technical term steady.

chapters.title: A Sacred Conception of Justice
comprehension_flags: The Platonic soul-part vocabulary — "concupiscent" and "irascible" for the appetitive and spirited faculties — is obscure to a general reader, and this pass is not authorized to add a gloss.
terminology_notes: al-Haqq / الحق — the divine name appears variously as the transliteration alone ("al-Haqq"), the script alone ("الحق"), and the two paired ("al-Haqq, الحق"); a book-wide convention for when script, transliteration, or both are shown would keep this central term consistent.
